title: The Godfather: The Horse's Head
description: A refused favor, a prized stallion, and a morning scream—Go Deep into Hollywood's worst wake-up call.

questions.question: When Hollywood mogul Jack Woltz refuses to cast Johnny Fontane, what does he wake up to find in his bed?
questions.explanation: Tom Hagen left dinner early—Mr. Corleone "insists on hearing bad news immediately." The Don's reply arrived by morning, under the sheets.

questions.question: That horse's head came from Woltz's prized stallion. What was its name?
questions.explanation: Woltz shows him off to Hagen and says he won't race him: "I'm gonna put him out to stud." Same name as Sudan's capital.

questions.question: Woltz boasts that Khartoum is how much money "on four hooves"?
questions.explanation: "I'll bet Russian czars never paid that kind of dough for a single horse," he brags. His pride showed the Don exactly where to hit him.

questions.question: The threat behind that 600-thousand-dollar lesson is the Don's line to Johnny Fontane: "I'm gonna make him..." what?
questions.explanation: Michael later explains: Luca Brasi held a gun to a bandleader's head while the Don promised "either his brains or his signature would be on the contract."

questions.question: After that offer he can't refuse lands in the bed, where did Coppola get the real head used on camera?
questions.explanation: One real head, packed in ice. Actor John Marley (Woltz) was not told it was real. His scream did the rest.

imageHint: A dark hand controlling puppet strings, suggesting the power and manipulation themes

deeperMode.title: Go Deeper: Behind the Camera
deeperMode.description: A director who thought he was getting fired, and an unscripted prop in Brando's lap

questions.question: Which director spent The Godfather's shoot convinced Paramount was about to fire him?
questions.hint: Winning the Patton screenplay Oscar mid-shoot made firing him awkward

questions.question: What animal did Coppola drop into Brando's lap without a word—never in the script, still purring on the soundtrack?
questions.hint: It purred so loudly Brando's lines needed ADR

easterEgg.title: The cat was never in the script
easterEgg.text: Coppola spotted a stray on set and dropped it in Brando's lap without a word. It purred so loudly that the Don's lines had to be re-recorded, and you can still hear it on the soundtrack.
